```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

tarshare lets independent `targets` pipelines reuse each other's results
through one shared cache directory. This vignette builds two small projects
that have never seen each other, points them at the same cache, and shows the
second one skipping the work the first one did.

## A cache

A cache is a directory that every pipeline can reach at the same path, usually
on shared storage. `shared_cache()` creates its layout and returns a small
configuration object that pipelines pass to `tar_shared()`. This vignette uses
a temporary directory so that it cleans up after itself.

```{r}
library(targets)
library(tarshare)

root <- tempfile("tarshare-vignette-")
dir.create(root)
cache_path <- file.path(root, "cache")
cache <- shared_cache(cache_path)
list.files(cache_path)
```

## Project A

A `_targets.R` that uses tarshare looks like any other, except that the step
worth sharing is declared with `tar_shared()` instead of `tar_target()`. It
takes the same name and command, plus the cache.

The vignette writes its scripts with `targets::tar_helper()`, which lets it
substitute the temporary cache path with `!!`. In a real project you would
simply type the path.

```{r}
script_a <- file.path(root, "project-a", "_targets.R")
dir.create(dirname(script_a))
tar_helper(script_a, {
  library(targets)
  library(tarshare)

  cache <- shared_cache(!!cache_path)

  summarise_values <- function(x) {
    cat("summarise_values() is running\n")
    c(mean = mean(x), spread = stats::sd(x))
  }

  list(
    tar_target(values, c(3, 5, 8, 13)),
    tar_shared(summary, summarise_values(values), cache)
  )
})
```

Run it in its own store:

```{r}
store_a <- file.path(root, "project-a", "_targets")
tar_make(script = script_a, store = store_a)
```

targets dispatched both targets as usual. For `summary`, tarshare printed a
`compute` line: nothing in the cache matched, so the command ran, printed its
own line, and the result was stored. The twelve hexadecimal characters after
`compute` are the start of the computation key.

```{r}
tar_read(summary, store = store_a)
```

## Project B

Project B is a different pipeline in a different directory with its own
store. It calls the target `summary_stats`, but the computation is the same:
the same helper applied to the same values.

```{r}
script_b <- file.path(root, "project-b", "_targets.R")
dir.create(dirname(script_b))
tar_helper(script_b, {
  library(targets)
  library(tarshare)

  cache <- shared_cache(!!cache_path)

  summarise_values <- function(x) {
    cat("summarise_values() is running\n")
    c(mean = mean(x), spread = stats::sd(x))
  }

  list(
    tar_target(values, c(3, 5, 8, 13)),
    tar_shared(summary_stats, summarise_values(values), cache)
  )
})

store_b <- file.path(root, "project-b", "_targets")
tar_make(script = script_b, store = store_b)
```

This time tarshare printed `hit` with the same key. The helper did not run,
and project B's store now holds the result that project A computed:

```{r}
tar_read(summary_stats, store = store_b)
```

Project B never read project A's metadata, and project A does not know that
project B exists. The only thing they share is the cache directory.

## What happened

`tar_shared()` is a target factory. It returns an ordinary target whose
command is `shared_run(<your command>, cache, ...)`. When targets dispatches
that target it loads `values` as it would for any target, then evaluates the
wrapper, which:

1. computes a key from the command's code, the values and functions it refers
   to, the packages involved, the declared context and the seed;
2. looks for that key in the cache's `actions/` directory;
3. on a hit, restores the stored result; on a miss, evaluates the command
   under a lock for that key and publishes the result.

targets then stores the value in its own store exactly as it would have done
without tarshare. The usual skipping still applies: run project B again and
targets does not even dispatch the target, so tarshare is not consulted.

```{r}
tar_make(script = script_b, store = store_b)
```

## The same cache from a plain R session

`shared_run()` is the function underneath `tar_shared()`, and a script can
call it directly with the same cache. The first call computes and stores,
and any later call with the same code and inputs is a hit:

```{r}
values <- c(3, 5, 8, 13)
summarise_values <- function(x) {
  cat("summarise_values() is running\n")
  c(mean = mean(x), spread = stats::sd(x))
}
shared_run(summarise_values(values), cache)
```

Each hit or computation is signalled by a message of class `tarshare_event`.
Handle it to log what the cache did:

```{r}
log_events <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, tarshare_event = function(e) {
    cat("cache:", e$event, "\n")
    invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
  })
}
log_events(shared_run(summarise_values(values), cache))
```

A `tar_shared()` target also folds a fingerprint of its declared `context`
into its key, so a plain `shared_run()` call and a pipeline target do not
share entries with each other even when their code is identical. Sharing
happens between pipelines, or between scripts that call `shared_run()` the
same way.

## When the code changes

Change the helper in project B so that it also reports the median. targets
notices that a dependency of `summary_stats` changed and dispatches it; the
key changes with the code, so tarshare computes:

```{r}
tar_helper(script_b, {
  library(targets)
  library(tarshare)

  cache <- shared_cache(!!cache_path)

  summarise_values <- function(x) {
    cat("summarise_values() is running\n")
    c(mean = mean(x), median = stats::median(x), spread = stats::sd(x))
  }

  list(
    tar_target(values, c(3, 5, 8, 13)),
    tar_shared(summary_stats, summarise_values(values), cache)
  )
})
tar_make(script = script_b, store = store_b)
```

Nothing is overwritten. Put the original helper back and the run is a hit
again, because the earlier result is still in the cache:

```{r}
tar_helper(script_b, {
  library(targets)
  library(tarshare)

  cache <- shared_cache(!!cache_path)

  summarise_values <- function(x) {
    cat("summarise_values() is running\n")
    c(mean = mean(x), spread = stats::sd(x))
  }

  list(
    tar_target(values, c(3, 5, 8, 13)),
    tar_shared(summary_stats, summarise_values(values), cache)
  )
})
tar_make(script = script_b, store = store_b)
```

Results accumulate until somebody runs maintenance deliberately. The
`vignette("operations")` guide explains who holds a result and how
unreferenced data is removed.
